Subject: Sponsorship invoicing + promo stacking for summer cohort

Hi Marissa,

Quick question from our sponsorship team — we’re running a summer accelerator (Jun–Aug) and a corporate sponsor wants to host the infrastructure cost for a set of teams. They’ve asked two things and I wanted to see if Redwood can accommodate:

1) Sponsor invoicing / fiscal hosting: can invoices be raised to the sponsor (Springbridge Capital) and consumption attributed to the cohort teams? They need a single monthly invoice for accounting.

2) Promo stacking: we were offered your standard free credits for each startup. The sponsor wants to combine those credits with a one-time sponsor discount (so the sponsor picks up any overage). Is it possible to stack Redwood promotional credits with a sponsor-applied discount on the same account or invoice?

We can share a sponsorship term sheet and the sponsor’s PO/W9 if that helps. Attaching the term sheet for context.

Would love a quick yes/no and any documentation we should prepare (Sponsor letterhead, Tax/EIN, signed addendum, etc.). Can hop on a 20-minute call if easier.

Thanks,

Looping in details from pricing/ops perspective.

Summary of options we can offer (high level):

- Option A — Sponsor-hosted invoice + promo stacking: We can invoice the sponsor directly and apply a promo credit line per team on the consolidated invoice. Practical constraints: the promo credit must be represented as a discount line item tied to the sponsor invoice; we can’t apply platform-level free credit to individual team accounts and also separately invoice sponsor for the same token line (double-counting risk).

- Option B — Sponsor covers overage only: keep per-team free credits intact; when a team exceeds credits we bill sponsor for those overages as a single monthly aggregated charge. Cleaner from revenue side, but sponsor will see variable monthly amounts.

- Option C — Dedicated committed discount: convert cohort to a reserved capacity / committed spend for the cohort period and provide a negotiated committed discount. This requires an MSA addendum and minimums, but makes billing predictable.

Operational asks from our side: sponsor PO, W9/EIN, billing address, and a sponsor-signed addendum allowing us to consolidate charges and apply discounts to a sponsor invoice. Also attaching a simple promo calculator I used to model a $5k sponsor contribution vs spend.

Laura — can you confirm tax/revenue recognition constraints and whether a $10k one-time sponsor credit applied as an invoice discount looks ok from Rev Ops (and whether we need to flag any ASC 606 notes)? Also, any concerns if sponsor wants promo stacking across N distinct internal accounts?

Ben Carter
Head of Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Thanks for the context. Finance/revenue ops take below.

We can support sponsor-hosted invoicing with promo stacking under the following conditions:

- Sponsor provides PO, W9 (EIN) and billing address. We need the Sponsor on file as a bill-to customer entity.
- Promo stacking allowed if we record the sponsor contribution as an invoice-level discount line tied to the sponsor account. We cannot record the same promotional value twice (i.e., both as free credit on startup accounts and as sponsor-paid credit).
- Suggested implementation: issue one consolidated monthly invoice to Sponsor with two line items — (1) gross consumption for cohort (aggregated), (2) sponsor discount / credit (negative line) tied to the Sponsor account. Revenue will be recognized net of the discount; please note this affects rev recognition timing under ASC 606.

Limitations and recommended cap: 
- For accounting simplicity and to avoid complex intercompany flows, cap sponsor top-ups at $10,000 per cohort by default. Larger amounts require a Rev Ops sign-off and potentially a contract amendment.

Required deliverables for setup: signed Sponsor Letter (sample attached), PO, W9/EIN, billing address. Once we have those we can: create the Sponsor bill-to account, wire up consolidated invoicing, and apply the contracted discount line. Also recommend sending DocuSign addendum for the sponsor hosting clause.

Link to internal billing playbook: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/REVOPS/pages/42679/Billing+Playbook

If you want, I can draft the short sponsor addendum (1 page) and a sample invoice pdf for Ayesha to preview. Happy to join a call tomorrow 11am PT.

Laura Bennett
